### thm-cofinality-basics — REFUSE
CURRENT TEXT READ: "[L8] Precomposing a function with a bijection onto its domain leaves its range unchanged, since $g \circ h$ has image $g[h[\mu]] = g[\beta]$ when $h : \mu \to \beta$ is onto; a strictly increasing map of ordinals is injective, and satisfies $\xi \le \eta \Rightarrow g(\xi) \le g(\eta)$, both by trichotomy ([[def-injection-surjection-bijection]], [[lem-ordinal-trichotomy]])." Also: "**Where the strictly increasing witness is spent.** Twice, and both times essentially: in step 1.3, to know that a witness of successor length would have a largest value; and in step 2.1, to know that $g$ preserves $\le$, without which the composite $g \circ k$ need not be cofinal."
ASSESSMENT: The repaired L8 is correct. `def-injection-surjection-bijection` says, “f is injective if f(x) = f(y) implies x = y” and defines surjectivity equivalently by the image being the codomain. `lem-ordinal-trichotomy` says exactly one of α ∈ β, α = β, and β ∈ α holds. Together with the displayed image computation, these license every clause of L8. The theorem and proof are otherwise correct, and the ai-altered tags agree with the listed [UCL source](https://www.homepages.ucl.ac.uk/~ucahcjm/ast/ast_notes_4.pdf). Refusal is required because the final Remark is false about the current proof: step 3.1 also spends strict increase, explicitly using injectivity of g to conclude that its range has cardinality β.
COLLATERAL: No broken dependency, fact label, or proof citation was found; the uncorrected false Remark is an independent defect elsewhere in the item.
STAMPS: `verification` contains only `precheck: pass`; there is no `judge`, `audited`, or `verified` stamp. That is honest after the material repair.

### thm-regularity-of-the-alephs — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "[L4] Every infinite cardinal is a limit ordinal (claim (b) of [[thm-cardinal-arithmetic-agrees-with-finite-counting]], [[def-limit-ordinal]]), and a cardinal $\kappa$ is infinite exactly when $\omega \subseteq \kappa$, that is $\omega \le \kappa$ ([[def-cardinal-arithmetic]], [[def-cardinal]])."
ASSESSMENT: L4 is correct and precisely sourced. `thm-cardinal-arithmetic-agrees-with-finite-counting` says, “Every infinite cardinal is a limit ordinal.” `def-limit-ordinal` says an ordinal is limit when it is nonzero and not a successor. `def-cardinal-arithmetic` says, “A cardinal κ is finite when κ ∈ ω and infinite when ω ⊆ κ, that is ω ≤ κ.” `def-cardinal` defines a cardinal as an ordinal not equinumerous with a smaller ordinal. The proof correctly uses these facts to establish regularity of the successor alephs under choice and singularity of aleph-omega in ZF. The title, Statements, Remarks, and ai-altered provenance agree with the mathematics and the listed [UCL source](https://www.homepages.ucl.ac.uk/~ucahcjm/ast/ast_notes_4.pdf).
COLLATERAL: none found
STAMPS: `verification` contains only `precheck: pass`; there is no stale `judge`, `audited`, or `verified` stamp. This is correct.

### cor-cofinality-of-a-cardinal-power — REFUSE
CURRENT TEXT READ: "$\\kappa < \\kappa^{\\operatorname{cf}(\\kappa)}$ for every infinite cardinal $\\kappa$, and $\\operatorname{cf}(2^{\\kappa}) > \\kappa$; in particular $\\operatorname{cf}(2^{\\aleph_0}) > \\aleph_0$" Also: "[L7] Every infinite cardinal is a limit ordinal, and a cardinal is infinite exactly when $\omega \le \kappa$ ([[thm-cardinal-arithmetic-agrees-with-finite-counting]], [[def-limit-ordinal]])."
ASSESSMENT: Two fatal defects remain. First, the title omits the Axiom of Choice although the Statement begins, “Assume the Axiom of Choice,” and `def-cardinal-arithmetic` says exponentiation is defined exactly when the relevant function set is well-orderable, becoming universally available under choice. The positive title therefore asserts more than the proof establishes. Second, L7 is incorrectly cited: `thm-cardinal-arithmetic-agrees-with-finite-counting` says only, “Every infinite cardinal is a limit ordinal,” while `def-limit-ordinal` merely defines limit ordinals. Neither states the infinite-cardinal criterion. Its actual source, `def-cardinal-arithmetic`, says, “A cardinal κ is finite when κ ∈ ω and infinite when ω ⊆ κ, that is ω ≤ κ.” That item is declared in `deps` but is not cited in L7. The underlying theorem is standard under choice and is supported by the listed [UCL source](https://www.homepages.ucl.ac.uk/~ucahcjm/ast/ast_notes_4.pdf), but the current title and Fact remain defective.
COLLATERAL: No removed label or dependency was found. L10’s least-upper-bound clause is an immediate elementary consequence of the cited ordinal facts and falls within the permitted short-gap triage.
STAMPS: `verification` contains only `precheck: pass`; there is no stale `judge`, `audited`, or `verified` stamp. The stamp removal is correct despite the unresolved content defects.

### fs-every-aleph-is-regular — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "[L2] An infinite cardinal $\kappa$ is regular when $\operatorname{cf}(\kappa) = \kappa$, and singular when $\operatorname{cf}(\kappa) \ne \kappa$ ([[def-cofinality]], [[def-cardinal]])."
ASSESSMENT: The repair exactly restores the missing domain and singular clause. `def-cofinality` says, “An infinite cardinal κ is regular when cf(κ) = κ” and “singular when cf(κ) ≠ κ.” `def-cardinal` defines the cardinal domain used there. The refutation then validly instantiates the false universal claim at omega and uses the cited theorem’s exact conclusion that aleph-omega has cofinality aleph-zero and is singular. The title and Remarks remain accurate, and the ai-altered provenance is consistent with the listed [UCL treatment](https://www.homepages.ucl.ac.uk/~ucahcjm/ast/ast_notes_4.pdf).

### fs-cardinal-exponentiation-is-strictly-monotone-in-the-base — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "The claim is plausible because the **weak** form is true — $\kappa \le \lambda$ does give $\kappa^{\mu} \le \lambda^{\mu}$ ([[lem-cardinal-arithmetic-basic-laws]]) — and because Cantor's theorem supplies the different strict inequality $\kappa < 2^{\kappa}$ at every cardinal ([[thm-cardinal-power-set-and-cantor]])." Also: "**The weak form is not damaged.** $\kappa \le \lambda \Rightarrow \kappa^{\mu} \le \lambda^{\mu}$ remains true, and so does Cantor's strict inequality $\kappa < 2^{\kappa}$."
ASSESSMENT: Both replacements are correct. `lem-cardinal-arithmetic-basic-laws` states that base comparison gives the corresponding weak comparison of powers. `thm-cardinal-power-set-and-cantor` states, “κ < 2^κ.” The text now correctly distinguishes those two results instead of misidentifying Cantor’s inequality as strict monotonicity in the exponent. The squeeze proving equal aleph-zero and aleph-one powers is valid, the title matches the false claim refuted, and the ai-altered provenance agrees with the exponent-collapse result in the listed [Harvard notes](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~wboney/fall16/settheory.pdf).
COLLATERAL: none found
STAMPS: `verification` contains only `precheck: pass`; no stale `judge`, `audited`, or `verified` stamp remains. This is correct.
